decision_cruda.rationale: LH-01 is down at C512-10 (radio and CMMS agree). Likely repair is 13:30, so 136 t at 13.4 g/t (about 58.6 oz) would sit idle for most of the shift. LH-08 comes from the cheapest source, the infrastructure heading at 0.5 oz/h, and is 0.69 h away. At 29.1 t/h it clears the stope in about 4.7 h, finishing around 15:00. Central trucks are not limiting (63 t/h inflow against 91 t/h capacity) and the stockpile has room. Cost is about 6 oz of development value, so net is about 50 oz. LH-09's heading is worth 2.0 oz/h and LH-07's stope is a producing one, so I left both in place.

Keep LH-08 on C512-10 (130 t at 13.4 g/t, about 56 oz, LH-01 down until about 13:30). Lend LH-09 from the preparation heading (2 oz/h) to N600-08 (165 t at 11.5 g/t, about 61 oz). Travel is 0.4 h. It loads about 85 t before LH-02 is repaired at about 13:40. That is about 21 oz more than waiting for LH-02 alone, against a heading cost of about 8 oz. Norte trucks have spare capacity (66 t/h against 42 t/h inflow). The infrastructure heading is already giving up LH-08. No reserves, because no stope is stopped.

Keep both loans: LH-08 at C512-10 (124t at 13.4 g/t, about 55 oz, finishes in ~4.3h) and LH-09 at N600-08 (160t at 11.5 g/t, about 59 oz, ~6.8h). Their dev cost is small (0.5 and 2.0 oz/h). The only uncovered stope is E569-01 (319t, about 106 oz), but every possible lender is a loading stope with ore to finish by 17:00. LH-07 would gain about 55 oz at E569-01 and lose about 36 oz at C590-14, plus travel time, so the net is about zero or negative. LH-10 is in PM until 14:00. Repairs are expected 11:50-14:50, so I will re-evaluate then. Nothing is in conflict between radio and CMMS.
